title: What Are the Most Central Parenting Behaviors in Interactions With Infants? A Network Analysis of the Coding Interactive Behavior Instrument.
abstract: Parenting has repeatedly been shown to have an important role in child development, and valid instruments assessing parent-child interaction quality are thus crucial for our understanding of parenting in child development. Network psychometrics is a novel approach to measurement validation in giving a more dynamic exploration of relations among relatively stable dispositions. The Coding Interactive Behavior (CIB) instrument is a global rating system of parent-child interaction quality, consisting of items averaged onto parenting composites. Studies have shown that these composites can be validated but are also liable to change due to contextual factors, making comparison across studies and contexts difficult. We investigate network analysis as an alternative to using these composites to understand parenting. The sample was 304 mother-infant and 303 father-infant dyads in a free-play interaction coded with the CIB. The results showed similar network structures for both mothers and fathers, yielding closely linked clusters of items for sensitivity, affect, and intrusiveness. Configural and partial metric invariance was established between the two networks. We also found the item Acknowledging to be the most central parenting behavior in the networks. Our results illustrate how a network analysis provides important information on multidimensional constructs and informs our understanding of the central and core elements of parenting of infants.
